variants.text: If I can avoid it, I don't want to live together early. Once we do, a bad relationship can start surviving because rent is expensive or one of us has nowhere easy to go. That's not evidence the relationship is working. The check-in date is mostly there so we don't wait until one of us is desperate to ask.

Living together early scares me for a very unromantic reason. Once two people share rent, a bedroom, furniture, maybe a pet, slowing the relationship down becomes a practical mess. Sometimes housing means you don't have much choice. But if I do have a choice, I don't want logistics deciding that the relationship continues. I also want a date when we ask each other how it's going before the answer is already a crisis.

I need to stop treating “I want to be with her” as an answer to questions it doesn't answer. Do I want to raise children with her? Live with her? Build a community with her? Those need their own answers. I also want to notice when “I’m taking a chance on this person” has quietly changed into “she’s the right person.” Maybe I learned something new. Maybe I just got more attached.

Wanting her is not the same question as whether I want her as my co-parent or life partner. I keep forgetting that because romance makes the first answer feel enormous. So when “I’m taking a chance on this person” turns into “this is the right person,” I want to know what changed. Did I actually learn something, or did the relationship just get harder to question?

And don't stop your own practices just because you're in love. If I stop reparenting and meditating because my partner makes me feel okay, then she's doing part of that job for me whether we say so or not.

I keep reparenting and meditating when I'm in love too. That's exactly when it's easy to stop, because somebody else is making me feel good. If I only remember how to regulate myself after the relationship is in trouble, I waited too long.
If something feels off, I slow down. I don't need to decide whether it's intuition or anxiety first. The point is just not to let being excited make me skip the question I was about to ask.

Sometimes the only thing I have is a little “wait” feeling. It doesn't prove anything. But if I'm about to ignore a question because I really want this to work, that's enough reason for me to ask the question before I keep going.
